questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a circular red light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a circular red light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a circular red light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing the lanes. What can you do?

options.text: Cross these lines only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: You can see cross traffic better.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your field of vision becomes smaller. When this happens, you need to stay extra alert for dangers around you.

questions.question: A vehicle is coming toward you with high beams on. Where should you look?

options.text: The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the other vehicle's lights and helps you stay on course until it passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a lane for left turns only. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: They are placed wherever there is danger.
They tell you what you must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn you about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They show speed limits, turn restrictions, and other driving rules you must follow.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection, let cross traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe. Which traffic light means this?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let cross traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: On a multilane road with traffic going both directions, when should you use the shared center lane?

options.text: To slow down or stop before turning left
To drive straight when traffic is slow

questions.correctAnswerText: To slow down or stop before turning left
questions.explanation: Use the center lane only to slow down or stop safely before making a left turn. Do not use it for passing or driving straight.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss than cars. They can hide in your blind spot, and it can be hard to judge their distance and speed. Always be alert and careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road's main travel area.
Force the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road's main travel area.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, give oncoming traffic at least half of the road's main travel area. Both vehicles need space to pass safely.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign tells you to slow down and give the right-of-way to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: Drivers should look ahead at least ____ seconds ahead of their vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 seconds
questions.explanation: Look ahead 12 seconds in front of your vehicle. This helps you prevent sudden stops or turns.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: You should leave more space than usual when stopping:
questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on a hill. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts, you will have room to avoid a crash.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: If traffic lights are not working due to a power outage, you should:

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers your plans.
Turn on your hazard lights and go through the intersection without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is out, treat it as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers just like you would at a four-way stop, then proceed with caution.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, shaded areas freeze faster. Trees and buildings block the sun, so these areas freeze first and dry last.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: To turn left on a multilane one-way street or highway, start from:
questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Stops the alcohol from affecting you.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot make you sober or reduce your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: When two tracks are next to each other, a second train may be coming on the other track. Watch for trains from both directions on both tracks before crossing.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Then gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up as you enter a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means what will appear soon?
questions.correctAnswerText: A steady red light
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver doesn't dim their high beams, where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the other vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight ahead in the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Rush ahead to pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. They have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn into or out of a driveway, or to turn left into or out of a highway (where allowed).

questions.question: When you see a work zone sign that says "45 mph where workers present," what should you do?

options.text: Drive safely for conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less where workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely for conditions, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less where workers are present.
questions.explanation: In these zones, you can drive at the normal speed limit when no workers are present. Slow to 45 mph or less only when you see workers to keep them safe.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not be able to stop in time.
